newsitem.title: USA: Zinc price hike to boost shares - equity analysts.
newsitem.headline: Zinc price hike to boost shares - equity analysts.

text.p: An expected sharp hike in zinc prices over the coming year has created several investment opportunities in zinc mining and refining companies, equity analysts said.

"We believe that the best selections for lower risk exposure, but strong gearing to a higher zinc price, are Pasminco and Cominco. Metaleurop represents the best higher risk leveraged exposure," SBC Warburg said in a detailed report on global zinc equities.
Also this week HSBC James Capel initiated coverage of Cominco with a buy recommendation.

"With robust demand, falling LME stocks and a dearth of new mine capacity, we are forecasting annual average prices of 55 cents per pound in 1997, 60 cents per pound in 1998 and 63 cents per pound in 1999," HSBC said.
"Cominco is well positioned to profit handsomely from the expected run up in zinc prices," HSBC added.
Warburg expected a dramatic rise in the zinc metal price from 46.5 cents per pound in 1996 to an average of 67.5 cents per pound in 1998, a 45 percent hike.
LME cash zinc prices officially settled at 54 cents a pound on Friday.

"Most of the zinc companies have seen some appreciation in their share price in early 1997 following a rally in the price of zinc to above 50 cents per pound," Warburg said. "However, given our expectation of further increases in the zinc price, we believe that there is still significant upside in the share price of most of the zinc stocks."
Metals analysts have noted a greater interest in zinc, especially among the funds in recent months as they savor the metal's turn in the limelight at last.
But investment in new mine and smelter capacity is expected to result in increased supplies and a more balanced market with lower real prices in 1999 and 2000.
Warburg said China still had the ability to unravel a major price hike in zinc.

"However, limitations on domestic ore supplies and imported concentrates, relatively few additions to future Chinese smelting capacity and a projected trend rate of domestic consumption growth of 5 percent are expected to curtail the growth in Chinese net exports between 1997 and 2000 to 250,000 to 280,000 tonnes per year," Warburg said.

Pasminco's intention to buy the huge Century deposit in Australia and Glencore International's growing presence in the market via the Iscaycruz mine in Peru, a stake in Metaleurop and most recently, becoming the largest shareholder in Asturiana de Zinc, are also seen by many in the industry as evidence of renewed confidence in the metal.

Huge stocks hampered zinc's ability to enjoy much of the recent base metals boom, but Warburg said the relative lack of new smelting capacity will result in stocks falling to critical levels during 1998, spurring the sharp rise in price.
LME zinc stocks Friday fell 125 tonnes to 476,600 tonnes.
